Use case: stylized-concept. Create a polished wide 3:2 two-panel creature concept board for Pantheon Realms. This is a radical anatomical redesign, NOT a recolor of a generic four-legged European dragon. Use painted dimensional classic fantasy strategy game creature rendering: natural textured scales and feathers, beautiful sculptural light, readable silhouette, restrained highlights, no photoreal film look, no cartoon. Dark slate-green quiet studio background, antique gold thin border, gold serif title and captions. Base creature on LEFT, upgrade of SAME SPECIES on RIGHT, equal panel sizes, similar scale and facing right at 3/4 side angle. Full body with all wings, tails and appendages well inside each half, no clipping/overlap. Both visibly WINGED in a grounded restful default pose, no airborne hovering, no action scene, no effects obscuring anatomy. The upgrade must introduce several immediately readable structural features: silhouette, crest shape, wing outline and tail structure, not just more saturation. Both share a recognizable core identity. Upgrade details are intentional fantasy game adaptations, not claims of historical depictions. No people, saddles, riders, menus or stats. Exactly one creature per half.
MYTHOLOGICAL BASIS: ZILANT, the winged serpent-dragon of Tatar/Kazan legend and heraldry, black body, red wings, golden talons and a crowned head. Anatomical identity: a dragon-serpent head on an upright S-curved neck, relatively compact birdlike thorax, exactly TWO powerful birdlike hind legs with golden raptor talons, NO forelegs and NO arms, a long tapering snake tail forming a graceful open loop behind the body and resting on the ground, and exactly TWO LARGE BAT-MEMBRANE WINGS attached to the shoulders. The two feet planted flat support the body; tail lightly braces it. Proud upright but restful stance, no lifted foot. Not a four-legged dragon. No feathered wings, no giant western dragon chest, no chicken head, no cobra hood. Exquisite midnight-black scales with subtle oil-blue iridescence, dark red leathery wing membranes. Reptilian horned long face with dignified fierce expression, amber eyes and restrained forked tongue. Both visible wings partly extended enough to see their outlines.
BASE LEFT: ZILANT. Streamlined black snake neck, a small three-point natural golden crest recalling a crown, modest red neck frill, smooth snake tail with a simple pointed tip, strong simple unbroken red membranes with four long wing digits.
UPGRADE RIGHT: CROWNED ZILANT. SAME BLACK-AND-RED palette and bipedal core anatomy, but dramatic tall openwork golden heraldic crown with five long points at head (a tasteful real crown is part of this species' myth-inspired identity); a pronounced backwards-pointing dark crimson neck fan; new secondary hooked thumbs at the two wing leading edges, broader deeply scalloped wings with an extra long outer membrane lobe creating a recognizably different outline; sturdy scaled gold talon sheaths; end of long snake tail develops an elegant three-bladed black-and-gold lance tip, completely visible. More regal, not obese. The crown, neck fan, hooked wing tips and lance tail must all clearly differ from base. Preserve black scales and red membrane, no fire breath or purple glow. TITLE "ZILANT". Left caption "ZILANT" with small "Base". Right caption "CROWNED ZILANT" with small "Upgrade".

MYTHOLOGICAL BASIS: CUÉLEBRE, the great winged treasure-guardian serpent of Asturian folklore. A feather-winged interpretation of the winged serpent; do NOT turn it into a European dragon or a Chinese dragon. Core anatomy: genuinely LEGLESS long substantial serpent, ZERO feet, ZERO arms, ZERO legs, ONE broad dignified reptile/dragon head, exactly TWO LARGE FEATHERED BIRDLIKE WINGS emerging from the upper body's sides. Wings have anatomically layered flight feathers, visibly NOT bat membranes. A long snake body rests in a low open coil on the ground, chest and neck rise from the supported coil like an alert resting cobra without a cobra hood. The body is weight-bearing on its grounded coils: clear floor contact shadows, no floating loops, no detached snake segments. The tail curves out from the coil and stays fully visible. Head is reptilian with subtle brow horns, not a bird beak; no whiskers, antlers or Chinese mane. Rich deep marine-blue scales with individually defined burnished copper edges, warm pearl belly scutes, amber eyes. Wings are steel-blue and warm ivory with copper edging. Half-raised wings show their feathery shape while keeping a tranquil default idle attitude. Fine craftsmanship and elegant dangerous beauty.
BASE LEFT: CUÉLEBRE. Simple smooth sinuous neck, modest paired swept brow horns, one layer of clearly separated primary flight feathers with rounded wing silhouette, plain tapering scaled tail, a restrained narrow feather collar behind jaw.
UPGRADE RIGHT: ANCIENT CUÉLEBRE. Preserve same legless coiled serpent body and SAME marine-blue, pearl and copper palette. Add an unmistakable swept-back broad fan of rigid ivory-and-copper crown quills behind head, stronger layered shield-like neck scutes, exceptionally long outer primary flight feathers and a second tier of spear-shaped shoulder feathers changing wing outline from rounded to elongated ceremonial form; tail ends in a clearly readable beautiful broad fan of five pearl-and-copper feathers instead of base's plain snake tip. Make old wisdom visible in head and heavier brow, but no human face. Keep fine rich scales, no coins embedded in hide, no enormous armor plates, no multiheads. The quill crown, neck guards, double-tier feather wings and tail fan are structural upgrade changes, clearly visible. Do not just recolor! TITLE "CUELEBRE". Left caption "CUELEBRE" with small "Base". Right caption "ANCIENT CUELEBRE" with small "Upgrade".
